title: Duel Decks: Knights vs. Dragons: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "Your signet is no symbol of power. It marks only your need for numbers to aid you. What do you do, guild-rat, now that you face my blade alone?"
"By tradition, we don't speak for two days after battle. If our deeds won't speak for themselves, what else could be said?"
Both guide and guard on open plain.
The skyhunters were born when the first leonin gazed at the heavens and wished to hunt the birds overhead.
"Hammer out your doubts as you forge your weapon. To slay a dragon, your resolve must be stronger than your steel."
Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the knight had just laid waste.
"He is part of a new breed of guardian, one who embraces the best of both his world and ours." —Mayael the Anima
Knight-stewards guard the Sun-Dappled Court, a grove of immense, sculptured olive trees that represent Valeron's twelve noble families.
"Command is the act of balancing on a vine and convincing others that it is firm ground." —Sidar Jabari
"If you think you are brave enough to walk the path of honor, follow me into the dragon's den."
Every elf in Shadowmoor is charged from birth with a terrible duty: to strike back against the ugliness and darkness, even though they are all around and seemingly without end.
Ambidexterity is common among kithkin. The thoughtweft links the minds of the left- and right-handed, giving each the knack of the other.
"Course he ran! *I* wouldn't want to stare down that barrel, either!" —Alaborn soldier
"We leonin have come to rule the plains by taking to the skies." —Raksha Golden Cub
The knights are a major attraction at every Lammastide festival. Teams of riders perform daring feats of flight to the delight of all below.
To protect the alliance between Kjeldor and Yavimaya, they trained in the ways of both.
Even when fate is already written, there's always time to change the names.
"Just as the noble soul calls virtue to itself, the evil soul summons harm." —Teachings of Eight-and-a-Half-Tails
"At harvest are seeds of next year sown."
"The southern fortress taken by invaders? Heh, sure . . . when elephants fly." —Brezard Skeinbow, captain of the guard
"Fear this no more!"
Those who survive the test bear a mark of power anyone can recognize.
"You helped save my people from a Phyrexian fate. Did you think I wouldn't return the favor?" —Eladamri, to Gerrard
"For unwavering commitment and unflinching strength, the Order of the White Orchid confers its sigil. Rise, knight-captain, and do your duty."
"Tusks to splinter skulls. Steel to shatter scale." —Warhammer inscription
It hardly weighs anything, but it takes all day to remove.
"The smell of roasted flesh hung over the valley for hours." —Onean sergeant
"I like goblins. They make funny little popping sounds when they die." —Braids, dementia summoner
Boggarts divide the world into two categories: things you can eat, and things you have to chase down and pummel before you can eat.
"My ears say it hisses. My fingers say it burns." —Auntie Wort
The oil sloshes against his skull as he nears his destination: the Frogtosser Games and the lighting of the Flaming Boggart.
"We speak the dragons' language of flame and rage. They speak our language of fury and honor. Together we shall weave a tale of destruction without equal."
Like so many Thran relics, the wurm engine kept operating long after its creators were gone.
In the erupting heart of Bogardan, it's hard to tell hurtling volcanic rocks from pouncing volcanic beasts.
A dragon's scale can be carved into a mighty shield, provided you can procure a dragontooth to cut it.
Sometimes primitive cultures attributed natural phenomena to monsters. Sometimes they were right.
The mysterious purpose of two of the rings had eluded Esper mages—until now.
Though no longer attached to the hand, it still holds its adversary in its grasp.
Goblins journey to the sacrificial peaks in pairs so that the rare survivor might be able to relate the details of the other's grisly demise.
"Within each of you is the strength of a landslide." —Kumano, to his pupils
"Kills and cooks your food in one easy stroke."
Only those gifted with the eye of Ugin, the spirit dragon, can see his fiery breath.
If your flesh can withstand the flame, the spirit of the dragon will burn within your soul.
"Life up here is simple. Adapt to the ways of the mountains and they will reward you. Fight them and they will end you." —Kezim, prodigal pyromancer
"Swords may sunder. Shields may fail. My will is stronger than steel, and my flesh and bone far more deadly."
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
When giants find their mountain homes infested, they have a whole range of solutions.
